newsitem.title: USA: Dollar soars against yen on weak Japan stocks.
newsitem.headline: Dollar soars against yen on weak Japan stocks.

text.p: The dollar soared against major currencies Monday as Japan's stock market plunge continued to depress the yen and on speculation that Germany would soon cut interest rates to revive a faltering economy.
The dollar rose to a high of 118.10 Japanese yen -- the highest seen since March 1993 -- as Tokyo's key Nikkei average fell 3.37 percent overnight.
The dollar also surged briefly above 1.6300 German marks in London -- the highest level since June 1994 as speculation increased of a possible German interest rate cut.

"It will be a continuation of two themes. The U.S. economy is growing well and it's a question of when, rather than whether, the Fed will raise rates," said IBJ International chief analyst Keith Edmonds in London.
"On the other side of the interest rate equation, the groundwork is being laid for a German interest rate cut."

Comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer and council member Hans-Juergen Krupp regarding Germany's economic struggles underscored the dollar's strong position vs. the mark and the rest of Europe, dealers said.

Tietmeyer warned in the International Herald Tribune that Germany's fledgling economic recovery was not yet self-sustaining and that a much-anticipated pick-up in growth could be delayed due to poor winter weather.
Krupp, meanwhile, addressed the negative consequences of German financial policy on economic growth in the run-up to European economic and monetary union.
However, the dollar's rally was checked by a partial U.S. holiday for Martin Luther King Jr. Day. The U.S. stock and commodity markets were operating normally.
"As soon as Europe closes, everybody will be out of here. Nothing is really going through. Dollar/mark will stay between 1.62 to 1.63," said Bob Near, a vice president at the Bank of New York.
"People are taking profits after the overnight highs, but the uptrend will resume as early as tomorrow when people get back to work," said a dealer at a European bank in New York.
In early afternoon trading, the dollar rose to 118.14 yen from 117.37 yen Friday, when it soared on news that the November U.S. trade deficit with Japan shrank 12.9 percent to $4.32 billion.
The dollar soared to 1.6281 German marks from 1.6182 marks. The dollar rose to 1.4145 Swiss francs for the first time since the summer of 1994 from 1.3993 late Friday.
